cards.explanation: The answer is across to the other side of the lake. Jesus says, “Let us cross to the other side of the lake.” Clear plan, clear destination, no confusion. I've gotten turned around between my own counter and my own oven, so a plan that clean impresses me.
The answer is False. The text says, “As they sailed, He fell asleep…” and then the windstorm comes down on the lake. So Jesus isn't awake the whole trip, friends. He's asleep when the weather turns.
The answer is True. The disciples went and woke Him. The boat was being swamped and they were in great danger, so they went to the one who was asleep. Nobody sat there waiting for a better moment.
The answer is rebukes. Jesus “…rebuked the wind and the raging waters…” Then they subsided, and all was calm. He doesn't sit and watch the storm, bakers. He gets up and speaks to it, and it settles.

The answer is frightened. The text says, “Frightened and amazed, they asked one another…” The storm is gone, but the fear isn't. Calm water, shaken disciples. I think they'd just seen something they couldn't file away anywhere.

The answer is who this man is. They ask, “Who is this?” They keep going: “He commands even the winds and the water, and they obey Him!” They've been in that boat with Him, and now they're asking who He is. That's a big question, friends, and it's a good one.
The answer is the tombs. The text says he “…stayed in the tombs.” No clothes and no house for a long time. That's a hard picture, and I think this one hurts.

The answer is Son of the Most High God. The man cries out, “What do You want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God?” He knows exactly who is standing in front of him, and he says it in a loud voice. The man is on the ground, but he gets the name right.

The answer is that he broke them. The text says, “…he had broken the chains…” They were chains and shackles, and still they didn't hold him. The text says he was driven by the demon into solitary places. I think this part of the story is heavy.

The answer is demons. The text says, “…many demons had gone into him.” So when he says “Legion,” it's because there isn't just one. The name tells you the crowd inside him. Jesus asks, and the man answers plainly.

The answer is to let them enter the pigs. The text says, “…the demons begged Jesus to let them enter the pigs…” Right before that, the demons kept begging Jesus not to order them to go into the Abyss (Luke 8:31). A large herd of pigs was feeding on the hillside. That's what they asked about.

The answer is True. The text says, “…He gave them permission.” The demons begged to enter the pigs, and Jesus gave His permission (Luke 8:32). Nothing is hidden in that verse, friends, so there's nothing to untangle. The text says it plainly, and so will I. True.

The answer is that the herd rushes into the lake and drowns. The text says, “…the herd rushed down the steep bank into the lake and was drowned.” This happens after the demons came out of the man and went into the pigs. It's a hard scene, and the text tells it plainly. Then those tending the pigs ran off and reported it in the town and countryside.

The answer is clothed. The text says he's “…clothed and in his right mind…” Earlier he hadn't worn clothing for a long time. Now he's sitting at Jesus' feet, dressed and thinking clearly. What a change, bakers.

The answer is True. The text says, “…they were afraid.” The people find the man sitting at Jesus' feet, clothed and in his right mind. I'd have expected cheering, but the text says fear. That's what they felt.

The answer is to leave their region. The text says, “…all the people of the region of the Gerasenes asked Jesus to depart from them, because great fear had taken hold of them.” The text gives their fear as the reason. So Jesus got into the boat and started back. That's how this stop ends.
The answer is False. The text says the man “…begged to go with Jesus. But He sent him away…” He doesn't get a seat in the boat, friends. Jesus gives him a job at home instead.

The answer is to go home and tell what God has done. Jesus says, “Return home and describe how much God has done for you.” The man had just begged to go with Jesus, and Jesus sends him home instead. Home, where he lived among the tombs before, is where he gets to tell it. And he does, proclaiming all over the town how much Jesus had done for him.
